title: dubai leads gulf gains uae saudi growth data lift sentiment 2026 09 03
text:
BENGALURU, Sept 3 (Reuters) - Gulf stock markets rose on Thursday, led by Dubai, as strong economic data in the United Arab ​Emirates and Saudi Arabia outweighed investor concerns over renewed U.S.-Iran clashes.
The latest attacks ‌marked the most substantial exchange of fire between the U.S. and Iran since July, with the war now in its seventh month.
UAE non-oil private-sector activity expanded in August at its fastest pace since December 2024, supported ​by sharper increases in output and new business, a survey showed.
Dubai's main ​index (.DFMGI)
, opens new tab
 rose 0.5%, with all sectors trading higher. Blue-chip developer Emaar Properties (EMAR.DU)
, opens new tab
 ⁠gained 1.1%, while Emirates NBD (ENBD.DU)
, opens new tab
, Dubai's largest lender, added 0.5%.
Abu Dhabi's benchmark index (.FTFADGI)
, opens new tab
 edged ​up 0.3%, led by gains in real estate and basic-materials stocks. Aldar Properties (ALDAR.AD)
, opens new tab
 rose ​0.9% and Space 42 (SPACE42.AD)
, opens new tab
 advanced 6.7%.
Saudi Arabia's benchmark index (.TASI)
, opens new tab
 advanced 0.2%, helped by gains in financial, IT and materials stocks. Saudi Arabian Mining (1211.SE)
, opens new tab
 rose 1.7%, and Riyad Bank (1010.SE)
, opens new tab
 gained 1.1%.
Saudi Arabia's non-oil private sector expanded at its ​fastest pace in six months in August, driven by stronger output as market activity ​recovered, a business survey showed.
National Shipping Company of Saudi Arabia (4030.SE)
, opens new tab
, known as Bahri, slipped 1.6%. Saudi ‌Arabia said ⁠on Wednesday that an Iranian attack on an oil tanker owned by Bahri had killed two Filipino seafarers. Qatar's benchmark (.QSI)
, opens new tab
 climbed 0.1%, supported by a 1.2% increase in telecommunication company Ooredoo (ORDS.QA)
, opens new tab
 . Gulf International Services (GISS.QA)
, opens new tab
, a Doha-based oilfield-services holding company, rose 3.8%.
Separately, three liquefied natural gas cargoes loaded in ​Qatar and the UAE ​have been transferred ⁠between ships outside the Strait of Hormuz in recent weeks for delivery to India and Japan, according to ship-tracking firms.
Outside the Gulf, ​Egypt's blue-chip index (.EGX30)
, opens new tab
 rose 1.1%, with almost all of its constituents ​posting gains. ⁠Commercial International Bank (COMI.CA)
, opens new tab
 added 1.5% and Talaat Moustafa Group (TMGH.CA)
, opens new tab
 climbed 1.2%.
Meanwhile, Egypt's economy grew 5.1% in the financial year 2025/26 compared to 4.4% a year earlier, according to a cabinet statement on ⁠Thursday.
